question: Who was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya in order to found the Maurya dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhana Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dhana Nanda was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty in ancient India.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya, with the guidance and support of his mentor Chanakya, defeated Dhana Nanda to establish the Maurya Empire.
 
• The Nanda dynasty was known for its substantial military strength and wealth, which was a significant challenge for Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The defeat of Dhana Nanda marked the end of the Nanda dynasty and the beginning of the Maurya Empire, one of the largest empires in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Maurya Empire and is considered one of the greatest rulers in Indian history.
 
• He was guided by Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, who was a brilliant political strategist and philosopher.
 
• Chandragupta's reign marked the unification of most of the Indian subcontinent under one central authority for the first time.
 
• He abdicated his throne in favor of his son, Bindusara, and became a Jain monk, spending his last years in Karnataka.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Dynasty**
 
 
• The Nanda dynasty ruled in northern India during the 4th century BCE, prior to the rise of the Maurya Empire.
 
• The Nandas were known for their significant military strength and extensive control over the Indian subcontinent.
 
• They maintained a large standing army and accumulated substantial wealth, which they used to maintain their power.
 
• The Nanda dynasty's rule was marked by substantial economic development and administrative control.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya**
 
 
• Chanakya was an ancient Indian teacher, philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• He authored the ancient Indian political treatise called the Arthashastra, which provides guidelines on governance, economics, and military strategy.
 
• Chanakya played a crucial role in the establishment of the Maurya Empire by mentoring and guiding Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Indian Machiavelli" for his political acumen and strategies.
